profile.headline: Australian henipavirus transmitted from flying foxes via horses; rare but highly lethal in humans.
profile.syndrome: Influenza-like illness progressing to pneumonitis or encephalitis; four of the seven recognised human cases died.
profile.transmission: Close contact with respiratory secretions and tissues of infected horses — all human cases have been horse-associated.
profile.diagnosis: RT-PCR and serology in high-containment laboratories.
profile.management: Supportive; m102.4 monoclonal antibody available on compassionate grounds.
profile.prevention: An equine vaccine (Equivac HeV) interrupts the transmission route to humans; PPE for veterinary work on sick horses.
evidence: Each human case virologically confirmed with an identified equine source since the 1994 Brisbane outbreak.

refs.label: Human Hendra virus encephalitis associated with equine outbreak, Australia, 2008. Emerg Infect Dis 2010

profile.headline: Bat-borne paramyxovirus with case fatality of 40–75% and documented person-to-person transmission; a WHO priority pathogen requiring BSL-4 handling.
profile.syndrome: Fever and headache progressing to encephalitis with brainstem signs, segmental myoclonus and seizures; acute respiratory distress is prominent in the Bangladesh/India lineage. Relapsing and late-onset encephalitis occurs months to years after recovery.
profile.transmission: Consumption of date palm sap contaminated by Pteropus bat secretions (Bangladesh/India), contact with infected pigs (the 1998–99 Malaysian outbreak), and person-to-person including nosocomial spread.
profile.geography: Malaysia, Singapore, Bangladesh, India (Kerala, West Bengal), Philippines.
profile.diagnosis: RT-PCR on throat swab, CSF, urine and blood; IgM/IgG ELISA — all in high-containment laboratories.
profile.management: Supportive intensive care. Monoclonal antibody m102.4 has been given compassionately; remdesivir is protective in primate models.
profile.prevention: Avoid raw date palm sap, cover sap collection pots, strict PPE and isolation for cases, pig-farm biosecurity. Vaccines are in clinical trials.
evidence: Repeated laboratory-confirmed outbreaks with genomic linkage between bats, intermediate hosts and patients, and documented nosocomial chains.

geo.text: Malaysia, Singapore, Bangladesh, India (Kerala, West Bengal), Philippines.

profile.headline: One of the most contagious human viruses (R0 of 12–18), vaccine-preventable, and a cause of lasting immune amnesia.
profile.syndrome: Prodromal fever, coryza, conjunctivitis and Koplik spots, then a confluent maculopapular rash. Complications: pneumonia, otitis media, diarrhoea, acute post-infectious encephalitis, and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis years later. Measles also deletes pre-existing antibody repertoires, raising susceptibility to other infections.
profile.transmission: Airborne — infectious aerosols persist for up to two hours in a room.
profile.geography: Worldwide, with resurgence wherever vaccine coverage falls below ~95%.
profile.diagnosis: IgM serology, throat/nasopharyngeal and urine RT-PCR for genotyping.
profile.management: Supportive; vitamin A reduces mortality in children.
profile.prevention: Two doses of live-attenuated measles vaccine (MMR); post-exposure vaccine within 72 hours or immunoglobulin within 6 days.
evidence: Definitive, with a century of clinical and virological data and global vaccine-impact evidence.

geo.text: Worldwide, with resurgence wherever vaccine coverage falls below ~95%.
